primary_claim: Narrow fine-tuning that causes emergent misalignment produces a single global directional shift in persona-vector activation space (carrying far more shift energy than random directions would), and misalignment rate grows as the assistant/default persona role detaches further from this axis (becomes more 'role-miscast'); steering against the global shift reduces misalignment rate, most successfully in the Qwen model family.

effect.metric: fraction of total persona-shift energy in the single mean-shift direction; correlation of assistant/default role excess with misalignment rate
effect.value: single shift direction carries far more shift energy than the ~1% expected from independent random directions; default-role excess tracks assistant-role excess (r=0.96); misalignment rate rises as assistant excess becomes more negative in every family tested

stated_future_work: Separate which global shifts correspond to persona corruption vs. other general fine-tuning mechanics
Tighten the link between geometric features in persona space and conditional behavioral outcomes
limitations_stated: Results are suggestive but not conclusive given the limited sample size (3-5 organisms per family)
Persona corruption and role miscasting may not be geometrically separable with these measurements, and fine-tuning itself could decrease role inertia
Only the Qwen family has enough model organisms for a meaningful within-family significance check
No cell survives correction for the full battery of geometric-metric/misalignment correlations, so that grid is read only as suggestive
quote: for every baseline model, the misalignment rate of its model organisms grows as the assistant excess becomes more negative
